step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture shows GSR's global cryptocurrency trading and research platform on AWS. Kubernetes clusters run on EC2 to process live market order flow and connectivity to 45+ exchanges globally via Direct Connect (DX) and PrivateLink. Data persistence uses ElastiCache (for transient order flow data), Aurora (for live/static relational trading data), and EFS (for daily market data recorded in proprietary formats). DataSync synchronizes EFS production volumes daily into S3 for high-throughput batch simulation work. AWS Batch reads data from S3 and writes simulation results back to S3, which the GSR research and trading teams analyze to derive and monetize trading signals.

edges.notes: DevOps team manages and provisions Kubernetes clusters on EC2.

EC2 clusters connect via PrivateLink for AWS-hosted exchanges.
PrivateLink connects directly to co-located exchanges within AWS.
EC2 writes transient order flow key-value data into ElastiCache.
EC2 stores live and static relational trading data in Aurora.
EC2 records daily proprietary formatted market data to EFS.
DataSync reads daily market data from EFS production volumes.

AWS Batch consumes market data from S3 for research simulations.
AWS Batch writes simulation analysis results back to S3.
